entities.summary: Peter of Zittau was a Bohemian churchman and historian. Born in Zittau, he entered the Cistercian monastery of Aula Regia (Zbraslav), founded by Wenceslaus II in 1292, and became the monastery's official historian. He is the primary author of the Chronicon Aulae Regiae. Esteemed by his colleagues, in 1316 Peter was elected the second abbot of Aula Regia. In this capacity he took part in the election of King John and staunchly opposed Henry of Carinthia. He later grew disenchanted with John, but wrote a lengthy lament for the passing of his wife, Elizabeth, the "true heiress of Bohemia", in 1330.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the primary author of the Chronicon Aulae Regiae, Peter's historical account provides valuable insights into the politics and society of medieval Bohemia. His role as abbot and historian also underscores his influence on the region's religious and cultural landscape.
